$comment: The source of sf-avatar-group's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/avatars (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

fields.summary: JSON text of the fields the attributes below also take (imageUrl, avatarUrl, avatarSize, active, check, name, source, labelText, labelSecondText, avatars, avatarsMore); an attribute wins over its field

property.summary: JSON text of the sizes the attributes round-size, label-size and profile-size also take

image-url.summary: The picture of the default, user and profile templates.

avatar-url.summary: The picture of the label template.

avatar-size.summary: The avatar's size step in the default and user templates (1/4 ... 3; the former words tiny, small, big and extra_big still read).

check.summary: Draws the verified badge on the default template's avatar.

name.summary: The person's name in the user template.

source.summary: The line under the name in the user template, with a link glyph: where the person comes from.

label-text.summary: The title of the label template.

label-second-text.summary: The line under the title in the label template.

avatars.summary: The group's avatars: an image, else its text (initials); the attribute takes the list as JSON text too

avatars-more.summary: The group template's last avatar: a number (drawn +N) or a short text for the people not shown.

round-size.summary: The avatars' size step in the group template (and in the default one when given).

label-size.summary: The avatar's size step in the label template.

profile-size.summary: The profile template's avatar size step: 2 or 3 (the former words small and big still read).

active.summary: Draws the online badge on the default template's avatar; check (verified) wins when both are set.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

user.$comment: The user combination of the one Lit template in JavaScript (§5.2 migration form), chosen by template="user".

group.$comment: The group combination of the one Lit template in JavaScript (§5.2 migration form), chosen by template="group".

label.$comment: The label combination of the one Lit template in JavaScript (§5.2 migration form), chosen by template="label".

profile.$comment: The profile combination of the one Lit template in JavaScript (§5.2 migration form), chosen by template="profile".

accessibility.$comment: Pictures beside visible text: each avatar is a span whose image has alt="" and is hidden from assistive technology; the visible text (name, label, the remainder) names the person or the group. Nothing takes focus.
accessibility.name: none

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-avatar-group for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.note: data is a reserved name; the shim maps the attribute and the property

rows.section: rename plan R0 (ui-control RENAME-PLAN-2026-11-03), naming decision 2026-11-02
rows.note: the element is sf-avatar-group; sf-avatars is a subclass defined beside it until the date

x-summary: Ready combinations of avatars: a person with a source, a stacked group with a remainder, an avatar with two lines of label, and a profile avatar with a verified badge. Drawn from sf-avatar's parts; for a single avatar with a name or a card use sf-avatar.
x-renamed: settings.data → fields: "data" is a reserved name (§3.1); data is its dated alias
x-decisions: a11y-role: none; a11y-name: none (the old shape "internal" meant the same). The avatars are pictures beside visible text -- the image alt="" and aria-hidden, the name, label or remainder printed -- and nothing takes focus; for an avatar that is a control use sf-avatar.

data -> fields: data is a reserved name (§3.1), so the JSON text of the fields is fields and data its dated setting alias (aliases.json, until 2026-12-01). It stays a string of JSON text, as the attribute always was; an attribute of the same field wins over it.

item-shape: avatars is a list whose entries are {image-url, text} (§4.2); image_url and initials are still read. The attribute takes the list as JSON text, as before; the property takes the list itself.
active is a value (out): the online dot the default template shows; it keeps its default, so a page that wrote active still writes the attribute.

templates: default, user, group, label and profile are the combinations of one Lit template in JavaScript (js/templates/default.js), the migration form §5.2 allows; the old template/*/index.html files are not compiled and stay as they were.
docs: the folder had no docs.md; it gains one (§3).

examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (the label combination: Команда проекта, 5 участников) plus a person with a source, a group with a remainder, a profile and the default with the online dot.

css-variables: the --sf-avatar-* public variables (five, seven since 1.2.3) of the class sheet sf-avatars draws with (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json, avatar), as sf-code-input declares the verification sheet's (§6).
version 1.1.0: a renamed member behind a dated alias is a minor (§4.10, §16.20).

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.

version 1.1.3: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.2.0: the tag is sf-avatar-group (naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>[-<variant>]); the folder, the id smart.avatar-group and the bundle cl-avatar-group follow it. sf-avatars stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: a subclass the Smart base defines beside the new tag, listed in the rule, in sheets as :is(sf-avatar-group, sf-avatars) (change journal tag-sf-avatars-to-sf-avatar-group, path-smart-avatars-to-avatar-group).

version 1.2.1: the profile example's first-paint snapshot is retaken after sf-avatar 1.2.3 (the verified badge plate and glyph are classes the class sheet paints from the palette); nothing of the group changes.

version 1.2.2 (2026-11-10): the offline dot of a member is the disabled ink laid over the place it stands on (C43, owner 2026-11-10; avatars 1.3.5): it read the muted ink, which became the translucent disabled ink in avatars 1.3.4 and let the photo show through. The bundle's sheet carries the avatars sheet, so this version records the change. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.2.3 (2026-11-10): the offline dot's two layers are public variables of the avatar sheet, --sf-avatar-offline-background-color (the place) and --sf-avatar-offline-overlay (the disabled ink over it; avatars 1.3.6): a page that sets the colour and the overlay none gets exactly that colour. The default look is unchanged. css-variables lists both. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.2.4 (2026-11-11, audit of dead Smart sheets): a patch, nothing drawn differently. The bundle no longer imports the avatars class sheet: its rule has no css, so the copy in smart/avatar-group/css/avatar-group.css never reached a page (force-linking it changed nothing on any snapshot, 1440 light/dark, 390); the avatars sheet comes by the rule's relation as before. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.2.5 (2026-11-12, avatar offline dot): a patch. A member's offline dot is the place's dim ink, not the disabled ink (avatars 1.3.7, the avatar sheet's defect fix, journal value-avatar-offline-dot-dim-ink).

version 1.2.6 (written on fix/content-precheck as 1.2.4; 2026-11-10, docs precheck AV-06): a patch. The group prints its overlap in the size names, sf-avatar-group--size-1/4, -1/3 and -1/2 (the --sf-space step of the overlap), in place of xs, sm and md, which stay dated aliases in component.avatars 1.4.0 until 2027-01-01 (journal class-avatar-group-overlap-size-names). Every setting has its summary. Every template draws sf-avatar's own parts (docs precheck smart content AG-01 measured on this pair: default 48, group 40, label 48, profile 56, user 40, all round). Drawn the same; settings, values, events and keys unchanged.
version 1.2.7 (2026-11-13, docs precheck smart content SC-S02): a patch, nothing drawn differently. active has its summary.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-avatar-group when the interface needs the avatars behavior.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component

accessibility.focus: Nothing here takes focus: every avatar is a decorative picture (alt ""), and the visible text names the person -- name in user, label-text in label. An avatar that opens a profile is an sf-avatar with aria-label inside the host's own link or button.
